points.title: 童年与早期教育
points.description: 文森特·梵高1853年3月30日出生于荷兰南部津德尔特的一个新教牧师家庭。他是家中六个孩子中的长子，性格内向而敏感。童年时期，梵高展现出对艺术的早期兴趣，但家庭更期望他从事宗教或商业工作。他的叔叔是一位艺术品商人，为梵高提供了接触艺术的机会。这段时期的生活对梵高后来的艺术观和人生选择产生了深远影响，尤其是他对贫困和苦难的关注。
points.descriptionEn: Vincent van Gogh was born on March 30, 1853, in Zundert, Netherlands, to a Protestant minister's family. As the eldest of six children, he was introverted and sensitive. During his childhood, Van Gogh showed early interest in art, but his family expected him to pursue religious or commercial work. His uncle was an art dealer, providing Van Gogh with opportunities to engage with art. This period profoundly influenced his later artistic views and life choices, particularly his concern for poverty and suffering.

points.title: 艺术商人与传教士
points.description: 梵高16岁时进入叔叔的艺术公司工作，先后在海牙、伦敦和巴黎工作。这段经历让他接触了众多艺术作品，但1873年因失恋而精神受挫。1876年，他放弃艺术商人职业，转而投身宗教，成为一名传教士。他在比利时矿区担任传教士，因同情矿工生活过于简朴而被教会解职。这一时期的经历使梵高对底层人民的苦难有了深刻认识，也促使他开始思考艺术与宗教的关系，为他后来的艺术创作奠定了思想基础。
points.descriptionEn: At 16, Van Gogh joined his uncle's art firm, working in The Hague, London, and Paris. This period exposed him to numerous artworks, but he suffered a mental breakdown after a failed love affair in 1873. In 1876, he abandoned art dealing to become a missionary. He served as a preacher in a Belgian mining district but was dismissed by the church for his excessive sympathy with the miners' harsh living conditions. These experiences gave Van Gogh a profound understanding of the suffering of the working class and prompted him to reflect on the relationship between art and religion, laying the groundwork for his later artistic creations.

points.place: 比利时布鲁塞尔、埃特莱赫
points.title: 艺术生涯的起点
points.description: 1880年，在弟弟提奥的鼓励下，27岁的梵高决定正式投身艺术。他前往布鲁塞尔学习绘画基础，随后回到荷兰家乡埃特莱赫。这一时期，他主要创作素描和早期油画，描绘农民和矿工的生活。他的作品风格受到荷兰现实主义画家米勒的影响，色调暗沉，笔触粗犷。1885年，他创作了早期代表作《吃土豆的人》，这幅作品展现了他对底层人民的深切同情。同时，他与家人关系紧张，尤其是与父亲的关系恶化，这促使他更加专注于艺术创作。
points.descriptionEn: In 1880, at the age of 27 and encouraged by his brother Theo, Van Gogh decided to pursue art formally. He went to Brussels to study the basics of painting, then returned to his hometown of Etten-leur in the Netherlands. During this period, he mainly created sketches and early oil paintings depicting the lives of peasants and miners. His style was influenced by Dutch realist painter Millet, featuring dark tones and bold brushstrokes. In 1885, he created his early masterpiece 'The Potato Eaters,' which demonstrated his deep sympathy for the working class. Meanwhile, his relationship with his family, particularly his father, deteriorated, prompting him to focus more on artistic creation.

points.title: 艺术革新与色彩探索
points.description: 1886年，梵高搬到巴黎与弟弟提奥同住，这是他艺术生涯的重要转折点。在巴黎，他接触到印象派和新印象派艺术，受到毕沙罗、德加、修拉等画家的影响。他的色彩变得更加明亮，笔触更加自由。他在巴黎创作了大量自画像和城市风景画，同时开始研究日本浮世绘艺术。这一时期，梵高的艺术风格逐渐形成，但他仍然感到孤独和不被理解。1888年，在弟弟提奥的经济支持下，梵高决定离开巴黎，前往法国南部的阿尔勒，寻求更明亮的光线和更纯粹的艺术表达。
points.descriptionEn: In 1886, Van Gogh moved to Paris to live with his brother Theo, marking a significant turning point in his artistic career. In Paris, he was exposed to Impressionist and Neo-Impressionist art, influenced by painters such as Pissarro, Degas, and Seurat. His colors became brighter and his brushstrokes freer. He created numerous self-portraits and cityscapes in Paris while also studying Japanese ukiyo-e prints. During this period, Van Gogh's artistic style gradually took shape, but he still felt lonely and misunderstood. In 1888, with financial support from his brother Theo, Van Gogh decided to leave Paris for Arles in southern France, seeking brighter light and purer artistic expression.

points.title: 创作高峰与精神危机
points.description: 1888年是梵高创作最丰产的时期之一。他在阿尔勒租下了一间黄色小屋，称之为'黄房子'，并邀请高更前来共同创作。在这里，梵高的艺术风格达到成熟，创作了《向日葵》、《夜间咖啡馆》等代表作。他的色彩更加鲜艳，笔触更加奔放，形成了独特的后印象派风格。然而，与高更的合作并不愉快，两人经常争吵。1888年12月，梵高在一次精神崩溃中割下了自己的耳朵，这一事件成为他人生和艺术生涯的转折点。这次事件后，他自愿进入精神病院接受治疗，但仍然坚持创作，完成了许多重要作品。
points.descriptionEn: 1888 was one of Van Gogh's most productive periods. He rented a small yellow house in Arles, which he called 'The Yellow House,' and invited Gauguin to join him there. In Arles, Van Gogh's artistic style reached maturity, creating masterpieces such as 'Sunflowers' and 'The Night Cafe.' His colors became more vibrant and his brushstrokes more expressive, forming a unique Post-Impressionist style. However, his collaboration with Gauguin was not harmonious, and they frequently argued. In December 1888, during a mental breakdown, Van Gogh cut off his own ear, an event that became a turning point in his life and artistic career. After this incident, he voluntarily admitted himself to a mental asylum for treatment but continued to create many important works.

points.title: 最后岁月与杰作
points.description: 1889年5月，梵高自愿进入圣雷米的精神病院接受治疗。在住院期间，他仍然坚持创作，描绘医院花园和周围的风景，创作了《星夜》等著名作品。1890年5月，在弟弟提奥的安排下，梵高前往奥维尔，由医生加歇照料。在奥维尔的最后两个月，梵高进入了创作的新高峰，每天创作一幅甚至多幅作品，包括《麦田群鸦》、《加歇医生肖像》等。然而，他的精神状况并未好转，1890年7月27日，他在田野中开枪自杀，两天后去世，年仅37岁。梵高一生创作了约900幅油画和1100幅素描，但生前只卖出过一幅作品。他的艺术成就直到死后才被广泛认可，成为现代艺术的先驱之一。
points.descriptionEn: In May 1889, Van Gogh voluntarily admitted himself to the asylum in Saint-Rémy for treatment. During his hospitalization, he continued to paint, depicting the asylum garden and surrounding landscapes, creating famous works such as 'The Starry Night.' In May 1890, at Theo's arrangement, Van Gogh went to Auvers-sur-Oise under the care of Dr. Gachet. In his final two months in Auvers, Van Gogh entered a new creative peak, producing one or more paintings daily, including 'Wheatfield with Crows' and 'Portrait of Dr. Gachet.' However, his mental condition did not improve, and on July 27, 1890, he shot himself in a field, dying two days later at the age of 37. Van Gogh created approximately 900 oil paintings and 1,100 drawings during his lifetime, but only sold one painting while alive. His artistic achievements were not widely recognized until after his death, establishing him as one of the pioneers of modern art.

supporter.zh: 梵高被视为艺术史上最伟大的天才之一，他的作品充满了原始的生命力和情感表达。支持者认为梵高的艺术超越了时代限制，开创了表现主义的先河，对20世纪现代艺术产生了深远影响。他的作品中的强烈色彩和情感表达，展现了对生活的热爱和对人性的深刻理解。梵高坚持艺术理想，即使在贫困和精神困扰中也不放弃创作，这种执着精神成为后世艺术家的楷模。他的艺术遗产不仅体现在作品本身，更在于他对艺术本质的探索和对人类情感的表达。
supporter.en: Van Gogh is regarded as one of the greatest geniuses in art history, whose works are filled with primal vitality and emotional expression. Supporters believe Van Gogh's art transcended the limitations of his time, pioneering Expressionism and profoundly influencing 20th-century modern art. The intense colors and emotional expression in his works demonstrate a profound love for life and deep understanding of human nature. Van Gogh's persistence in pursuing his artistic ideals, despite poverty and mental struggles, has become a model for later artists. His artistic legacy is not only reflected in his works themselves but also in his exploration of the essence of art and expression of human emotions.

critic.zh: 批评者指出梵高的作品存在技术上的局限性，他的构图和透视常常不符合传统艺术规范。一些评论家认为梵高的精神疾病影响了他的创作判断，使他的作品缺乏理性思考。此外，梵高生前未获得认可，部分原因可能是他的艺术风格过于前卫，不符合当时的主流审美。批评者也质疑梵高与他人的关系处理能力，尤其是与高更的合作失败，反映了他性格中的偏执和难以相处的一面。这些批评者认为，梵高的传奇形象很大程度上是后人构建的神话，而非完全基于历史事实。
critic.en: Critics point out technical limitations in Van Gogh's work, as his compositions and perspectives often deviated from traditional artistic norms. Some commentators suggest that Van Gogh's mental illness affected his creative judgment, making his works lack rational thinking. Additionally, Van Gogh's lack of recognition during his lifetime may be partly due to his avant-garde style not conforming to mainstream aesthetics of the time. Critics also question Van Gogh's ability to handle relationships, particularly his failed collaboration with Gauguin, reflecting his paranoid and difficult personality. These critics argue that Van Gogh's legendary image is largely a myth constructed by later generations rather than being entirely based on historical facts.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，梵高被定义为一位悲剧性的艺术天才，他的生平和作品已成为现代文化的重要符号。学术界将梵高定位为后印象派的关键人物，他的艺术风格对表现主义、野兽派等现代艺术流派产生了深远影响。流行文化中，梵高常被描绘为 misunderstood genius（不被理解的天才），他的故事被改编成电影、书籍和歌曲，成为艺术界最具辨识度的形象之一。梵高的作品，尤其是《星夜》和《向日葵》，已成为全球艺术教育的经典案例。他的生平经历，包括精神困扰和早逝，进一步强化了他在公众心目中浪漫化的艺术家形象，使他成为艺术与疯狂、天才与悲剧交织的文化符号。
objective.en: In academic circles and popular culture, Van Gogh is defined as a tragic artistic genius whose life and works have become important symbols of modern culture. Academia positions Van Gogh as a key figure in Post-Impressionism, with his artistic style profoundly influencing modern art movements such as Expressionism and Fauvism. In popular culture, Van Gogh is often depicted as a misunderstood genius, his story adapted into films, books, and songs, making him one of the most recognizable figures in the art world. His works, particularly 'The Starry Night' and 'Sunflowers,' have become classic examples in global art education. His life experiences, including mental struggles and early death, have further reinforced his romanticized image as an artist in the public consciousness, making him a cultural symbol where art intersects with madness, and genius with tragedy.

self.zh: 我越来越相信，创造美好的代价是努力、失望以及毅力。首先是努力，然后是毅力。
self.en: I increasingly believe that the price of creating beauty is effort, disappointment, and perseverance. First effort, then perseverance.

others.zh: 梵高是一位伟大的画家，他比我们任何人都要更深刻地理解色彩。
others.en: Van Gogh was a great painter who understood color more profoundly than any of us.
